claims.statement: The European Commission's PVGIS provides open solar-radiation and photovoltaic-performance data plus APIs suitable for automated expected-yield baselines.
IEA PVPS operation-and-maintenance guidance treats monitoring, forecasting, performance analysis, and performance indicators as core PV O&M activities.

contrary_evidence: Many inverters already ship with free monitoring portals, so generic dashboards have little value.
Residential owners may tolerate modest underperformance rather than pay a monthly fee.

economics.acquisition_route: Validate on 20-50 systems from the family-company network, then sell one fleet deployment to an inverter distributor or installer group.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 30000 active sites at 30 PLN monthly net revenue yield 10.8m PLN ARR; at 30% EBITDA, 4x EBITDA, and 65% founder ownership, business equity is about 8.4m PLN in year 5-7. This counts equity only and does not double-count retained earnings.
economics.founder_time: Hypothesis: 12-18 hours weekly for the first 12 months, with installer staff performing all site visits.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 75-85% software gross margin after telemetry, support, and channel share once integrations are stable.
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 120-300 PLN activation and support cost per site, recovered in 5-10 months of net subscription revenue.
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 39-59 PLN per site per month retail, with 20-30% retained by the installer; no field-service cost is included.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Hypothesis: four-year average retention because the alert history and warranty record remain tied to the system; annual service events reinforce value.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Normalized fault signatures, confirmed causes, and repair outcomes improve triage across inverter and installation types
fingerprint.customer: Residential and small-commercial PV owners served by regional installers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Installers and inverter distributors bundle activation into handover, warranty, and annual-service workflows
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: White-label monitoring, triage, and warranty-evidence subscription with field work billed separately by the installer
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Owner pays a recurring monitoring fee at installation or maintenance renewal; installer receives a disclosed share
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A newly commissioned or aging PV system produces less than weather-adjusted expectations or develops an intermittent fault

founder_fit: Parents' renewable-energy installer can supply a bounded, trusted pilot and operational feedback.
Weather normalization, anomaly detection, and automated triage match the founder's data-science skills.
A reseller-led sale avoids a consumer personal brand and can be operated part-time before scale.
risks: False alerts could create service cost and installer distrust.
Inverter vendors can restrict API access or change schemas.
Warranty wording could accidentally imply a financial production guarantee.

structure.control_point: Weather-normalized system health record and service-dispatch evidence
structure.critical_dependency: Installer cooperation and reliable access to inverter telemetry

thesis: Give solar installers a white-label, recurring service they can attach at handover: weather-normalized yield monitoring, loss alerts, remote triage, and a warranty evidence log. The installer already owns the customer relationship and earns a revenue share while avoiding undiagnosed underperformance; the software company accumulates a cross-fleet failure-and-remediation dataset without operating a field-service workforce.
title: Installer-Wrapped Solar Yield Assurance
uncertainties: Which inverter APIs are stable enough for a low-support pilot?
Will installers sell the service at handover or include it only in premium maintenance plans?
How much avoided truck-roll cost can be demonstrated in one Polish installer fleet?
